title: Error Correction
subtitle: Your mistakes from the 20 November class, plus the homework

slides.title: 1. The right preposition
slides.question: Which preposition goes with this word?
slides.summary: Many of your mistakes were prepositions: important to me (not with me), unhappy with something, related to (not related with), open up to someone (not with), a need for money (not about) and besides (no to after it).

expressions.meaning: it matters to that person: important to me.
not satisfied with a person or a situation.
connected to something. Not "related with".
talk honestly about your feelings to someone.
a situation where something is necessary.
in addition to. No "to" after besides.

items.question: Say what matters to you.
items.explain: important TO someone expresses an opinion or feeling.

items.question: Describe someone who is not satisfied.
items.explain: be + unhappy + WITH. Unhappy is an adjective, so it needs the verb be.

items.question: Explain what an argument was about.
Talk about an honest conversation at work.
blocks: I finally opened up to my boss
items.explain: open up TO someone ABOUT something.

items.question: Add one more thing.
items.explain: Besides = in addition to. No "to" after it.

slides.title: 2. Verb patterns
slides.question: What form comes after this verb?
slides.summary: Some verbs decide the form of the next verb: avoid + -ing (avoid bothering), need to + base verb (need to patch things up, not patching), agree to + base verb, and it depends on (not I depends on).

expressions.meaning: after avoid, use the -ing form: avoid bothering.
need to patch, need to improve. No -ing.
third person: it depends, always followed by on.
agree to help. Not "agree for helping".

items.question: Talk about being considerate at work.
blocks: I try to avoid bothering people

items.question: Talk about making peace.
blocks: we need to patch things up

items.question: Say you can't answer yet.
blocks: I can't give you an answer now

items.question: Talk about help from a colleague.
blocks: She reluctantly agreed to help me

slides.title: 3. Word forms and sentence structure
slides.question: Is the sentence built correctly?
slides.summary: Small structure mistakes: there are with plural nouns (not there is a children), no extra it after the subject (Loyalty is, not Loyalty it's), the adverb frequently (not frequency), the noun disagreement, and the time at the end of the sentence.

expressions.meaning: there is for one thing, there are for many.
don't add it after the subject.
describes a verb: communicate more frequently.
after a / small we need a noun.
We had a small disagreement this week.

items.question: Say what matters most in a friendship.
items.explain: The subject is loyalty: no "it" after it. Uncountable → is.

gloss.pt: a lealdade é… sem repetir o sujeito

items.question: Talk about a small problem this week.
items.explain: Subject + verb + object, then the time.

slides.title: 4. Correct the mistakes
slides.question: Can you fix each sentence without looking?
slides.summary: Your teacher's Exercise 2: rewrite each sentence correctly. Each one has at least one mistake from the points above: need to + base verb, agree to, there are, open up to and patch things up.

expressions.meaning: need to + base verb, not need to improving.
agree to + base verb, not agree for helping.
plural noun → there are.

expressions.en: open up to someone about something
expressions.meaning: open up TO a person.
need TO + base verb.

items.question: Talk about a manager's support.
blocks: My manager agreed to help me

practice.explain: important TO someone, when you give an opinion or a feeling.
practice.prompt: Loyalty is very important ___ me.

practice.explain: unhappy WITH someone or something.
practice.prompt: He is unhappy ___ his situation.

practice.explain: related TO something. "Related with" is a common mistake.
practice.prompt: Their argument was related ___ money.

practice.explain: open up TO someone.
practice.prompt: She opened up ___ her manager.

practice.explain: a need FOR something. Not "a need about".
practice.prompt: There is a need ___ more money in the project.

practice.explain: Besides (with -s), and no "to" after it.
practice.prompt: Beside to my job, I also study English at night.
accept: Besides my job, I also study English at night.
Apart from my job, I also study English at night.

practice.explain: After avoid, use the -ing form.
practice.prompt: I avoid ___ people when they are busy.

practice.explain: need to + base verb: need to patch things up.
practice.prompt: We need to ___ things up.

practice.explain: it → depends (with -s). Your sentence "I depends on" mixed I with the -s form.
practice.prompt: It ___ on the situation.

practice.explain: agree to + base verb.
practice.prompt: Build the sentence: after the argument.

practice.explain: Children is plural → there are.
practice.prompt: There ___ several children in the garden.

practice.explain: We need an adverb to describe the verb communicate: frequently.
practice.prompt: We communicate more ___ now.

practice.explain: After "a small" we need a noun: disagreement.
practice.prompt: We had a small ___ last week.

practice.explain: Don't add "it" after the subject loyalty.
practice.prompt: Loyalty it's the most important thing to me.
accept: Loyalty is the most important thing to me.
Loyalty is the most important thing for me.

practice.explain: Subject + verb + object, then the time: …a small disagreement this week.
practice.prompt: We had this week a small disagreement.
accept: We had a small disagreement this week.
This week we had a small disagreement.
This week, we had a small disagreement.

practice.explain: need to + base verb: improve.
practice.prompt: I need to improving my relationship with my colleagues.
accept: I need to improve my relationship with my colleagues.

practice.explain: agree to + base verb: agreed to help.
practice.prompt: She reluctantly agreed for helping me.
accept: She reluctantly agreed to help me.

practice.explain: Three children = plural → there are.
practice.prompt: There is three children in the house.
accept: There are three children in the house.

practice.expr: open up to someone about something
practice.explain: open up TO someone.
practice.prompt: I opened up with my husband about my problems.
accept: I opened up to my husband about my problems.

practice.explain: need TO + base verb: need to patch things up.
practice.prompt: We need patching things up after the disagreement.
accept: We need to patch things up after the disagreement.
